framework_notes.eu-ai-act: Read in the consolidated text of 27 July 2026. Its requirements bind the providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems: a cell applies only when the team provides such a system, and OpenGuildKit governs the coding agents that build it, not the system. Articles 9 (risk management), 12 (record-keeping) and 14 (human oversight) were read and left empty: they ask the high-risk system itself to manage its risks, record its events and be overseen, which a tool around coding agents does not do.
framework_notes.iso-iec-42001: Not read: the standard is sold by ISO, and its public page (https://www.iso.org/standard/42001) refused an automated read on 2026-11-28; no clause is filled.
framework_notes.nist-ai-rmf: Read in NIST AI 100-1 (January 2023), the tables of the GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE and MANAGE functions. A subcategory is an outcome for the organization: OpenGuildKit supplies part of the evidence, never the policy. No MEASURE subcategory is filled: OpenGuildKit measures nothing about an AI system.
framework_notes.soc-2: Not read: the Trust Services Criteria of the AICPA are downloaded behind an account of aicpa-cima.com (page seen on 2026-11-28); no criterion is filled.
framework_notes.dora: Read in the text published in the Official Journal (L 333, 27.12.2022). It binds financial entities: each filled cell is a part of Article 8 or 9, and the policies, the risk assessment and the approval by management lines these articles ask for stay with the entity.
framework_notes.nis-2: Read in the text published in the Official Journal (L 333, 27.12.2022). A directive binds through the law of each Member State, and Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690, which details the measures for some entities, was not read.

controls.title: A person approves a task before an agent works on it
controls.guarantees: task decide --approve needs the person to type the task ID at an interactive terminal, or, in a project with signed approvals, an SSH signature by an approver (a board removal is still typed at the terminal); without either the command is refused and the task stays reviewed.
controls.not_covered: It does not identify the person behind the terminal: the name is the one typed with --by.

maps_to.quote: procedures for the management of modifications to the high-risk AI system
maps_to.gap: Approves each agent task before work; the written strategy and procedures of the quality management system stay with the provider, and a change made without a task is not covered.

maps_to.quote: Processes for human oversight are defined, assessed, and documented
maps_to.gap: The approval before work is defined and its record documents it; assessing the oversight process, and the organizational policy behind it, stay with the organization.

maps_to.quote: all changes to ICT systems are recorded, tested, assessed, approved, implemented and verified in a controlled manner
maps_to.gap: Gives the approval of agent tasks; the documented, risk-based change policy approved by management lines, and the testing, stay with the entity.

maps_to.quote: security in network and information systems acquisition, development and maintenance
maps_to.gap: Holds agent work in development behind an approval; the other measures for acquisition and maintenance stay with the entity.

controls.title: Edits through the agent host are refused until an approved task covers them
controls.guarantees: With guard enforce and a host that has hooks (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI), the hook before an edit refuses it with exit code 2 unless a task whose approval still holds covers it; guard observe flags the edit and lets it through.
controls.not_covered: A shell command does not go through the hooks, and a host without hooks has none: guard --ci is then the only barrier. host check and host scan say which tools have no hook.

maps_to.quote: procedures for the management of modifications to the high-risk AI system
maps_to.gap: Refuses agent edits no approved task covers, only through hosts with hooks and under guard enforce; shell commands are not seen.

maps_to.quote: Mechanisms are in place and applied, and responsibilities are assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems
maps_to.gap: Stops an agent edit outside an approved task; it does not judge the performance of the agent, and shell commands and hosts without hooks pass.

maps_to.quote: all changes to ICT systems are recorded, tested, assessed, approved, implemented and verified in a controlled manner
maps_to.gap: Keeps agent edits under an approval in hosts with hooks; shell commands and hosts without hooks are not controlled, and the policy stays with the entity.

controls.title: An approval is sealed over what was approved
controls.guarantees: The approval carries a SHA-256 seal over the consultation, the review, the rules in force, the approver, the reason and the Git revision; a record changed after its export, or approved under other rules, no longer holds, and check, task list --decisions and guard --ci say so.
controls.not_covered: A local seal is not a signature: an agent that writes files can forge a record and compute its digests again. The completion of a task is checked for consistency, not sealed by a person.

controls.title: In a signed project an approval carries an SSH signature checked against the committed signers
controls.guarantees: With approvals in signed mode, task decide --approve needs an SSH signature of the decision payload by an approver; ssh-keygen verifies it against the allowed signers file as Git holds it at HEAD, and guard --ci verifies each record against the signers of the base revision.
controls.not_covered: It shows that a key listed in the signers file signed. Who holds the key, and how it is kept, is outside OpenGuildKit.
commands: profile set approval signed --signers PATH --approver NAME

maps_to.quote: all changes to ICT systems are recorded, tested, assessed, approved, implemented and verified in a controlled manner
maps_to.gap: Ties an approval to a key of the committed signers file; who holds the key, and the change policy, stay with the entity.

controls.title: The person who asked for the work does not approve it (option, off by default)
controls.guarantees: With separate-requester on in the profile, every new task names its requester, task decide refuses an approval by that person, and guard --ci refuses a record whose approver is its requester when the base revision has the option on.
controls.not_covered: Off unless a person turns it on. Names are compared without case or spaces, and a signed approval compares the requester to the signer's principal: a requester named otherwise than their principal is not caught.

maps_to.quote: Policies and procedures are in place to define and differentiate roles and responsibilities for human-AI configurations and oversight of AI systems
maps_to.gap: Keeps the requester from approving, when a person turns the option on; defining the other roles and the policy stay with the organization.

controls.title: A change must come with a valid exported decision, judged under the rules of the base revision
controls.guarantees: guard --ci checks each file changed since the base against the exported records the change brings; the mode, the profile, the catalog lock and the allowed signers come from the base revision, so a pull request cannot weaken the rules it is judged by.
controls.not_covered: That the check must pass before a merge is a setting of the Git host, which OpenGuildKit does not read.

maps_to.quote: procedures for the management of modifications to the high-risk AI system
maps_to.gap: Checks each changed file against an approved record before merge; making the check required is a setting of the Git host, and the written procedures stay with the provider.

maps_to.quote: all changes to ICT systems are recorded, tested, assessed, approved, implemented and verified in a controlled manner
maps_to.gap: Verifies that each change brings a valid approval, under the rules of the base revision; it runs no test, and requiring the check before merge is a setting of the Git host.

maps_to.quote: security in network and information systems acquisition, development and maintenance
maps_to.gap: Verifies in CI that each change of the repository was approved; it covers the repository only, not acquisition or the systems in production.

controls.title: An approval can be exported as a record the team commits
controls.guarantees: task export writes .openguildkit/decisions/ID.json with the approval payload, its signature, the brief, the board verdicts and a SHA-256 of the whole record; trace and task list --decisions read every record, teammates' included, and say whether it still holds.
controls.not_covered: Work done without a task has no record: guard --ci then reports a missing decision. A record exported outside Git lists no files and covers no path.

maps_to.quote: A description of relevant changes made by the provider to the system through its lifecycle
maps_to.gap: Records each approved task with its brief and reviews; work done without a task has no record, and the description of the system as a whole stays with the provider.

maps_to.quote: systems and procedures for record-keeping of all relevant documentation and information
maps_to.gap: Keeps the approval records of agent tasks in the repository; the other documentation of the quality management system is outside OpenGuildKit.

maps_to.quote: all changes to ICT systems are recorded, tested, assessed, approved, implemented and verified in a controlled manner
maps_to.gap: Records each approved agent task in the repository; changes made without a task, and outside the repository, are not recorded.

controls.title: An approval holds only under the rules it was given under
controls.guarantees: The approval records the fingerprint of the rules, checks and boards in force; when they change the approval no longer holds, check exits 1 and the hook stops covering edits with it. check also fails when the instructions of the project no longer match its profile and its catalog lock.
controls.not_covered: Only a change of the rules, checks and boards voids an approval: the guard mode, the host, the research setting, the approval mode and the waiver policy leave approvals standing.

controls.title: Each change to the profile records who made it, when and why
controls.guarantees: Every profile command appends its change, the person, the day and the reason to changes in .openguildkit/project.json; a change that lowers a protection (guard, signed approvals, public research) is typed by a person at an interactive terminal.
controls.not_covered: A hand edit of project.json is not an entry: Git holds it, and OpenGuildKit does not read that history except for the signers file.
commands: profile set guard enforce --by INITIALS --reason WHY

maps_to.quote: systems and procedures for record-keeping of all relevant documentation and information
maps_to.gap: Records who changed the settings of OpenGuildKit, when and why; a hand edit of project.json is not an entry.

maps_to.quote: including changes to software, hardware, firmware components, systems or security parameters
maps_to.gap: Records the changes to the protections of OpenGuildKit itself, with who, when and why; the security parameters of other systems are outside it.

controls.title: Dependency alerts are kept with who decided what, and a confirmed critical alert blocks approval
controls.guarantees: alerts import merges the reports of the project's scanners (npm audit, pip-audit, OSV-Scanner, GitHub Dependabot) into .openguildkit/alerts.json; severity, status, acceptance and dismissal record who, why and when; a confirmed critical alert that no person accepted blocks the approval and the completion of its tasks.
controls.not_covered: It reads the reports it is given and runs no scanner: a dependency no report lists is not in the register.

maps_to.quote: High-risk AI systems shall be resilient against attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter their use, outputs or performance by exploiting system vulnerabilities
maps_to.gap: Keeps the known vulnerabilities of dependencies that scanner reports list, with decisions; it runs no scanner and does not address attacks specific to AI.

maps_to.quote: AI risks and benefits from third-party resources are regularly monitored, and risk controls are applied and documented
maps_to.gap: Documents decisions on vulnerabilities of third-party packages from the reports it is given; it does not monitor the AI risks or benefits of third-party models.

maps_to.quote: assess cyber threats and ICT vulnerabilities relevant to their ICT supported business functions
maps_to.gap: Keeps the vulnerabilities that scanner reports list for the repository; it assesses no threat and runs no scanner.

maps_to.quote: including vulnerability handling and disclosure
maps_to.gap: Handles the vulnerabilities of dependencies that reports list; disclosure is not covered.

controls.title: The agent tools, MCP servers and instruction files of a repository are listed and scanned
controls.guarantees: host scan lists the agent tools whose files the repository holds, the MCP servers they configure and the permissive settings, and reports hidden characters, phrases that cancel the rules and downloads piped into an interpreter in the files an agent reads; projects --surfaces lists them for a folder of repositories.
controls.not_covered: It reads files, offline: a tool with no file in the repository cannot be seen, and what an agent does is not observed.

maps_to.quote: recourse to pre-trained systems or tools provided by third parties
maps_to.gap: Lists the agent tools and MCP servers configured in the repository; how they were used, integrated or modified, and the models behind them, are not described.

maps_to.quote: Mechanisms are in place to inventory AI systems
maps_to.gap: Lists the agent tools whose files a repository holds; a tool with no file there is not seen, and the resourcing is organizational.

maps_to.quote: Financial entities shall identify all information assets and ICT assets
maps_to.gap: Lists the agent tools and MCP servers configured in repositories; other ICT assets, and their criticality and links, are outside it.

maps_to.quote: asset management
maps_to.gap: Lists the agent tools and MCP servers configured in repositories; the other assets are outside it.
